brief:
An engineer in Gaza has begun constructing shelters for animals using discarded metal cans, according to Al Jazeera English. The project repurposes refuse materials to create housing for stray animals in an area facing severe constraints on available resources and building materials.

The initiative reflects efforts by residents to address both animal welfare and broader humanitarian needs through creative reuse of waste. With conventional shelter materials scarce, the engineer's approach allows basic structures to be assembled from everyday discarded items found throughout the territory. The work has drawn attention as an example of improvisation in response to resource limitations.
dek: Gaza engineer builds animal shelters out of empty cans.
title: Gaza engineer builds animal shelters from empty cans
